'''Naeem Ahmad Khan''' {{post-nominals|list=[[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|FPAS]]}} (12 April 1928 – 29 September 2013) was a Pakistani nuclear physicist and professor of physics.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences "/> Although he worked with the [[Government of Pakistan]] for most of his career, he also taught physics at a number of Pakistani universities and was a civilian scientist of the [[Pakistan Air Force]] (PAF) until his death.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences "/>

==Early life and education==
Khan was born in [[Hoshiarpur]], [[Punjab Province (British India)|Punjab]], British India on 12 April 1928.<ref name="Obituary published by NM Butt">{{cite journal |last1=Butt, PhD |first1=N. M. |authorlink1=Noor Muhammad Butt |title=Obituary: Dr. Naeem Ahmad Khan, FPAS |journal=Proceedings of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences |date=30 September 2013 |volume=50 |issue=4 |pages=347–348 |url=http://paspk.org/wp-content/uploads/proceedings/50,%20No.4/781cef36Obituary%20Prof.%20Naeem%20Ahmad%20Khan.pdf |accessdate=2 May 2020 |publisher=Pakistan Academy of Sciences Press |location=Islamabad |language=en-us |issn=0377-2969}}</ref> He enrolled at the University of Delhi and attended [[St. Stephen's College, Delhi|St. Stephen's College]], where he received a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree with honors in mathematics in 1946.{{rp|346}}<ref name="Dar Publications, Reza, 1990">{{cite book |last1=Reza |first1=S. Mohammad |title=Persons who Shape Our Destiny: A Compendium of Bio-datas of Those Persons who are Rendering Important Services in Various Fields of National Activity |date=1990 |publisher=Dar Publications |location=Lahore, Punj, Pakistan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=e25mAAAAMAAJ&q=Mathematics |accessdate=2 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref>{{rp|228}}<ref name="Harrap Research Pub., Haslett, 1963">{{cite book |last1=Haslett |first1=Arthur Woods |title=World Nuclear Directory |date=1963 |publisher=Harrap Research Pub. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FdE5AQAAIAAJ&q=Naeem%20 |accessdate=2 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref> Khan then joined the Indian Meteorological Department (Indian Met Office), transferring to the [[Pakistan Meteorological Department]] after the [[Partition of India|partition of India and the independence of  Pakistan]] in 1947.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences ">{{cite web |title=IAS » Prof. Naeem Ahmad Khan |url=http://www.iasworld.org/prof-naeem-ahmad-khan/ |website=www.iasworld.org |publisher=iasworld |accessdate=3 May 2020 |language=en-us |archive-date=21 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421133015/https://www.iasworld.org/prof-naeem-ahmad-khan/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Khan left the Pakistan Meteorological Department in 1948 to attend Sindh University in Hyderabad, where he received a Master of Arts (MA) degree in mathematics in 1950.{{rp|231}}<ref>{{cite book |title=International Who's who in Energy and Nuclear Sciences |date=1983 |publisher=Longman Group Limited, Professional and Information Publishing Division |isbn=978-0-582-90110-0 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QCBRAAAAMAAJ&q=%20MA%20(Sind) |language=en}}</ref> He joined the Pakistan Air Force (PAF) the following year, was commissioned as a lieutenant, and was a senior instructor in Air Force education units.{{rp|102}}<ref name="Biographical Research Institute, Pakistan, for International Publishers (Pakistan)">{{cite book |title=Biographical Encyclopedia of Pakistan |date=1970 |publisher=Biographical Research Institute, Pakistan, for International Publishers (Pakistan) |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zWxmAAAAMAAJ |accessdate=3 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref> Becoming interested in physics, Khan transferred to the Air Force Reserve to attend the physics program at Karachi University in 1953.{{rp|102}}<ref name="Biographical Research Institute, Pakistan, for International Publishers (Pakistan)"/>

Khan received a Master of Science (MSc) degree in physics (with research focused on mass spectroscopy) from Karachi University in 1955, and obtained funding from the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) to pursue doctoral studies in physics in the United Kingdom the following year.{{rp|175}}<ref>{{cite book |title=Energy & Nuclear Sciences International Who's who |date=1990 |publisher=Longman |isbn=9780582039681 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6SBRAAAAMAAJ&q=naeem+ahmad+khan+spectroscopy+1958+manchester |accessdate=3 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref>{{rp|231}}<ref>{{cite book |title=International Who's who in Energy and Nuclear Sciences |date=1983 |publisher=Longman Group Limited, Professional and Information Publishing Division |isbn=978-0-582-90110-0 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QCBRAAAAMAAJ&q=%20MA%20(Sind) |accessdate=3 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences Press Publications ">{{Cite web
 |title        = Khan, Naeem Ahmad
 |work         = Pakistan Academy of Sciences Press Publications
 |url          = http://www.paspk.org/fellow5.htm
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20070810193641/http://www.paspk.org/fellow5.htm
 |archive-date = 10 August 2007
 |url-status   = dead
 |df           = dmy-all}}</ref> He attended the [[University of Manchester]] and received a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree in nuclear physics in 1958.{{rp|288}}<ref name="Harrap Research Pub., Haslett, 1963" />{{rp|8}}<ref name="PAEC atomic scientists">{{cite book |last1=Commission |first1=Pakistan Atomic Energy |title=Pakistan's Atomic Scientists |date=1961 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_B9N5Rk5rgkC&q=naeem+ahmad+khan+Manchester+University |accessdate=3 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In 1959, he became a fellow of the [[Physical Society of London]].<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences" />

==<span class="anchor" id="Scientific career"></span>Career==
===Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission===
Khan returned from England and joined the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) in 1960. Promoted as a scientific officer the following year, his early research focused on low-energy nuclear reactions. Khan then returned to the United Kingdom,{{rp|31}}<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Riazuddin, PhD |first1=Dr. |authorlink1=Riazuddin (physicist) |editor1-last=Khan, PhD |editor1-first=Hameed A. |editor2-last=Qureshi, PhD |editor2-first=M. M. |editor3-last=Hussain |editor3-first=Tajjammul |editor4-last=Haye |editor4-first=Irfan |editor2-link=Mazhar Mahmood Qurashi |editor3-link=Syed Tajammul Hussain |title=50+5 Years of Physics in Pakistan |journal=COMSATS' Series of Publications on Science and Technology |date=1 April 2006 |volume=8 |issue=6 |pages=217 |url=http://comsats.org/Publications/Books_SnT_Series/08.%20Physics%20in%20Developing%20Countries%20-%20Past,%20Present%20and%20Future%20(April%202006).pdf |accessdate=3 May 2020 |publisher=M/s A.R. Printers |location=Islamabad, Pakistan |language=en-us |quote={{small|''Fifty five years of Physics in Pakistan have been analyzed from a personal perspective. Successes and failures, together with their causes, are also discussed. The current trends in development of Physics are also mentioned.''}}}}</ref><ref name="Obituary published by NM Butt" /> where he conducted his postdoctoral research at the [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment]] in Harwell (funded by the PAEC and the [[United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority]]).{{rp|8}}<ref name="PAEC atomic scientists" /> He was a research fellow at the [[Franklin Institute]] in Philadelphia in 1964 and 1965.{{rp|102}}<ref name="Biographical Research Institute, Pakistan, for International Publishers (Pakistan)" />

Khan returned to Pakistan in 1965, and was a senior scientific officer at the PAEC Minerals Center in [[Lahore]]; he became its principal scientific officer in 1967.<ref name="Obituary published by NM Butt" /> He formed the Nuclear Physics Group, with mechanical engineer [[Hafeez Qureshi]], physicists [[Sultan Bashiruddin Mahmood|Bashiruddin Mahmud]] and [[Samar Mubarakmand]] as key members.{{rp|2–3}}<ref>{{cite book |title=Proceedings of the Pakistan Science Conference |date=1968 |publisher=Pakistan Association for the Advancement of Science. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fJxWAAAAMAAJ&q=Naeem%20Ahmad%20Khan%20 |accessdate=3 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref> The Nuclear Physics Division made fundamental calculations on [[neutron scattering]] through the [[gas centrifuge]] process before it was disbanded by 1969.<ref name="The Nation, 2007">{{cite news|last1=Mahmood|first1=Sultan Bashiruddin|title=Hafeez Qureshi: A great scientist passes away|url=http://nation.com.pk/.|accessdate=10 November 2014|agency=The Nation|publisher=The Nation, 2007|date=15 August 2007|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141111013721/http://nation.com.pk/|archivedate=11 November 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Khan was posted to the PAEC's administration in 1970, and was its director of training and international affairs before becoming secretary.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences" /> His research continued to focus on developing a solid-state nuclear track detector, and he aided work on neutron scattering; in 1968, he published an article on the subject with Qureshi.{{rp|2}}<ref>{{cite book |title=Proceedings of the Pakistan Science Conference |date=1968 |publisher=Pakistan Association for the Advancement of Science. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fJxWAAAAMAAJ&q=Naeem+Ahmed+Khan+Hafeez+qureshi |accessdate=7 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref> Khan was appointed director of the Research Technological Department in 1975, directing the Nuclear Physics Division before becoming director of the Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology (Pakistan's national laboratory) in 1977.<ref name="Obituary published by NM Butt" /><ref>{{Cite web | title =Professor Dr. Naeem Ahmed Khan| website =| date =| url =http://www.radaris.com/US/show-people/?name=Naeem| doi =| accessdate =}}{{dead link|date=February 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}
</ref>

===<span class="anchor" id="Chair PCSIR, academia and Government of Pakistan"></span>Academic and government work===
Khan became chairman of the Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (PCSIR) in 1984, where he remained until he became technical adviser to the Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation (COMSTECH) in 1989.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences "/> He was a founding fellow of the [[Islamic World Academy of Sciences]] in 1986, promoting science and technology in the Islamic world.<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences "/> Khan left COMSTECH in 1996. He was also vice-president of the [[Pakistan Academy of Sciences]] (PAS).<ref name="Islamic Academy of Sciences "/>

In 1997, Khan became a professor of physics at Karachi University, Sindh University in Hyderabad, [[Quaid-i-Azam University|Quaid-e-Azam University]] in Islamabad, [[University of the Punjab|Punjab University]] in Lahore, and the Air University in Islamabad.<ref name="Obituary published by NM Butt" /> He supervised five doctoral candidates in physics at Punjab University who were funded by the PAEC.<ref name="Obituary published by NM Butt" />

Khan also worked for the [[Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division)|Ministry of Energy]] (MoE), and briefly served on the advisory board of the [[Hydrocarbon Development Institute of Pakistan]].<ref name="Obituary published by NM Butt" /> In 2007, he became the Pakistan Air Force's (PAF) civilian scientist, instructing its pilots on aerodynamics and meteorology at the [[Pakistan Air Force Academy]] in Risalpur.<ref>
{{Cite web
 | title =  Naeem A. Khan
 | url =  http://www.ias-worldwide.org/profiles/prof37.htm
 | archive-url =  https://web.archive.org/web/20110610134200/http://www.ias-worldwide.org/profiles/prof37.htm
 | archive-date =  10 June 2011
 | url-status =  dead
 | df =  dmy-all}}</ref> Khan died in Islamabad on 29 September 2013, and is buried there.<ref name="Obituary published by NM Butt" /> Physicist [[Noor Muhammad Butt|N. M. Butt]] published a eulogy and obituary for the PAS in October 2013.<ref name="Obituary published by NM Butt" />

==Research in physics==
Khan's research revolved around the [[Medical physics|biological applications]] of nuclear physics. He worked in [[nuclear fission product|fission production calculations]] and energy measurement through the solid-state nuclear track detector (SSNTD), which he wrote in 1989 with "Solid State Nuclear Track Detection: A Useful Tool for Basic and Applied Science Research" (co-authored with Hameed Ahmad Khan.<ref>

}}
